claim: For the one-parameter three-round two-way LOCC protocol for minimum-error discrimination of the equiprobable double-trine ensemble introduced by Chitambar and Hsieh, with Alice's first-round measurement strength \(p\in[0,1]\), the total error probability is exactly \[E(p)=1-\frac12\left(Q(p)+\sqrt{S(p)}\right),\]where \[Q(p)=\frac{8+2\sqrt3+(\sqrt3-2)p}{12}\]and \[S(p)=\frac{20+8\sqrt3+(4+8\sqrt3)p-(3+4\sqrt3)p^2}{48}.\]This protocol family has a unique global minimizer \[p_*=\frac{45-8\sqrt3}{39}=0.798553680498\ldots,\]with exact minimum error \[E_*=\frac{63-32\sqrt3}{117}=0.0647382406649\ldots.\]The endpoint \(p=1\) is the optimal one-way protocol with error \(E_{\to}=1/2-\sqrt3/4\), so the explicit feedback protocol's exact advantage is \[E_{\to}-E_*=\frac{11\sqrt3-18}{468}>0.\]The claim optimizes only this published one-parameter adaptive protocol family; it does not claim the globally optimal finite-round or unrestricted LOCC error.

correctness.rationale: The source branch probabilities and postmeasurement states give \(P_0=(1-p)/3\), \(P_1=(2+\sqrt3)(2+p)/12\), and \(c=(1-p)/(2(2+p))\). The Helstrom expression simplifies to the displayed \(E(p)\). The exact stationary equation factors as \((p-1)((18+11\sqrt3)p-(14+9\sqrt3))/216=0\) after squaring; the unsquared sign condition rejects \(p=1\), and endpoint derivative signs make the remaining root the unique global optimum.

value.rationale: The source protocol is the explicit finite-round witness for a strict two-way-over-one-way communication advantage. Its exact calibration \(p_*\), exact error, and exact positive gap replace a plot-level numerical witness with a reproducible closed-form benchmark. This is a natural protocol invariant with direct operational meaning, not an arbitrary parameter slice.
